newsitem.title: CANADA: CN sees improving operating performance.
newsitem.headline: CN sees improving operating performance.

text.p: Canadian National Railway Co expects to meet its operating ratio target of 83 percent for 1997, Chief Executive Paul Tellier said on Wednesday.
"We are well positioned to achieve our target in 1997," Tellier told Reuters from New York, where he was meeting with analysts.
"The operating ratio trend line keeps moving in the right direction," he said.
CN has set an operating ratio target of 83 percent for 1997, compared with 85.6 percent in 1996.

Operating ratio measures operating expenses, net of financing charges, as a percentage of revenues. It is a standard for measuring the overall performance of a railway. The lower the ratio, the better the railway's performance.
Tellier declined to make a profit forecast for the year, but said he was pleased with the increase in the railway's revenues and net income in the first quarter.
CN reported a net profit of C$128 million or C$1.51 a share in the first quarter, versus year earlier C$82 million or C$0.97 a share.
CN's operating ratio improved to 85.1 percent from 87.3 percent. The operating ratio figures excluded a charge of C$16 million in last year's first quarter.

CN's first-quarter results showed an 11 percent increase in intermodal revenues and a 10 percent increase in automotive revenues. Grain and grain product revenues were up by seven percent, despite difficult weather conditions in western Canada.
Tellier said that despite tough weather conditions in the first quarter in Canada, the railway posted record volumes almost on a daily basis in February and March.
"The business is there. The volume is pretty good," Tellier said.
"I think we are well positioned for the rest of the year," he said.
